---
title: "Running Benchmarks"
---

Every run is described by three words. A **suite** is a workload domain such
as `slm` or `vision`. A **workload** is one benchmark ID. A **profile** is the
run scale. That is the entire user-facing vocabulary.

## Profiles

| **Profile** | **Meaning** | **Use it for** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `min` | Minimum representative run, one small path per suite | Install check, smoke test, classroom demo, CI |
| `max` | The full benchmark suite at the standard comparable scale | Course assignments, artifact evaluation, paper baselines |
| `pro` | Research envelope exposing controlled variants and knobs | Architecture, backend, quantization, and serving studies |

`min` proves it runs, `max` runs the suite, `pro` opens the research space.
Comparable numbers come from `max`; results from `min` are smoke signals, not
scores.

## Selecting What Runs

A bare `--profile` selects that profile's default path. `--suite` narrows to
one domain, `--workload` selects one benchmark family, and `--variant` narrows
to a single variant within it.

```bash
mlperf run --profile min                      # default min path, all suites
mlperf run --suite vision --profile max       # one suite
mlperf run --workload nanogpt-train --profile max
mlperf run --workload smollm2-chat-inference --variant quantized-int8 \
    --profile max --model smollm2-135m
```

Add `--dry-run` to any of these to print the selection without running it.
Model-backed workloads accept `--model <alias>`; each benchmark page lists the
aliases its family supports.

## Fetch Before You Measure

```bash
mlperf fetch --workload resnet18-train --profile max
mlperf fetch --profile max --dry-run     # preview all downloads
```

`fetch` downloads datasets and model weights, verifies hashes, and populates
the cache so the measured run contains no network time. `mlperf cache list`
shows what is on disk.

## Reports and Output

Runs write JSON, HTML, and CSV reports plus a `.provd` provenance artifact.
Use `--output-dir` to choose the destination and `--open-report` to open the
HTML report on completion. Reports include hardware and software fingerprints,
dataset and model dossiers, and quality-target status; the
[results guide](results.qmd) covers how to read, verify, and package them.

## Power Telemetry

```bash
mlperf run --workload dscnn-kws-train --profile max --power
```

`--power` adds aggregate estimated watts and joules to the report using
`powermetrics` on macOS or `nvidia-smi` on CUDA machines, without requiring
privileged hardware counters. Treat the numbers as coarse energy telemetry
for systems reasoning, not as calibrated power measurements.

## Reproducibility Basics

Runs are seeded and dataset recipes are deterministic. For comparable results
across machines or submissions, always use `--profile max`, report the
generated fingerprint block unmodified, and keep the `.provd` artifact with
the result. Score-bearing workloads additionally enforce the quality target
declared on their benchmark page.
